beats.narration: Letting a frontier model hand selected subtasks to a cheaper worker scored higher than the frontier model alone on ViBench, at lower cost. The caveat: the evidence comes from a single model pairing per benchmark and small held-out sets.
beats.on_screen: Delegating subtasks: better score, lower cost, thin evidence

beats.narration: Running a frontier agent on every step is expensive. This paper asks whether the lead can delegate only the parts where a weaker worker is good enough, without training an orchestrator.
beats.on_screen: Route parts of a task, not the whole task

beats.narration: Offline, the lead and worker each solve tasks alone. An LLM annotator labels recurring subtasks in those traces, and an LLM judge scores each model on each subtask. A parameter called delta turns quality and cost savings into delegate, conditional or keep tiers, which go into the lead's prompt.
beats.on_screen: Annotate traces, judge subtasks, set tiers with delta. Profiling cost about $30

beats.narration: At the main delta setting, the ViBench score rose to seventy-eight point five at nineteen percent lower cost than the lead alone. On Terminal-Bench the pass rate was sixty point nine percent, the highest of any method. The plan alone, with no worker, cut the lead's cost by thirty-nine percent on ViBench and sixteen percent on Terminal-Bench.
beats.on_screen: ViBench 78.5 at 19% lower cost. Terminal-Bench pass rate 60.9%

beats.narration: The Terminal-Bench gain rests on a small held-out set with no significance testing, so it amounts to a few task outcomes. Whether it holds for model pairs with smaller gaps is untested, and the judge was not validated against human labels. Delegation also adds time: the median Terminal-Bench task took sixty-nine minutes.
